_meta.purpose: Everything the site needs to know about the affiliate relationship, and the licence constraints that bind the machinery. Values here are either supplied by the operator, derived from a fetched primary source (see source), or null because nothing official confirms them.

brand.name: Counter Tested
brand.tagline: Small kitchen appliances, picked the slow way.
brand.blurb: We publish buyer questions, comparison dimensions and the paperwork behind each recommendation. When we have not confirmed something, the page says so instead of guessing.
voice_rules: Second person, plain words, no hype adjectives.
Never claim hands-on testing that did not happen.
Every number on the page has a source row or is blank.
Say what we do not know before we say what we think.
brand.why_this_name: Chosen in this session. Nothing in the repo defined a brand; the brief only fixed the tracking ID. Rename in one place: data/program.json -> brand, then rebuild.

site.published_from: GitHub Pages, deployed by .github/workflows/deploy.yml from the committed site/ folder produced by tools/build_site.py
site.note_on_base_url: Relative URLs are used in every page, so the site also works from a file:// preview and from any custom domain without a rebuild; absolute URLs appear only in canonical tags, the sitemap and the RSS feed.

associates.implied_associates_id_basis: Amazon's help text says the software automatically appends "-20" to Associate IDs [S25]. This is an arithmetic observation about the supplied string, not a confirmed account identifier.
associates.tag_format_rule: XXXXX-## must appear as a URL parameter on every link placed on the site [S03]

api_access.why_null: PA-API/Creators API credentials are account-held; nothing in this repo or environment carries them. Qualifying-sales and application status are also unknown [S17].

join_clock.rule: 3 qualifying sales within 180 days of application, or the application can be withdrawn and the account cannot be reinstated [S17].
join_clock.why_null: The application date is not in the repo and cannot be read without account access. Operator must enter it: python3 tools/campaign_ledger.py program --application-date 2026-11-XX

required_disclosures.associate_statement: As an Amazon Associate I earn from qualifying purchases.
required_disclosures.amazon_content_disclaimer: CERTAIN CONTENT THAT APPEARS ON THIS SITE COMES FROM AMAZON. THIS CONTENT IS PROVIDED ‘AS IS’ AND IS SUBJECT TO CHANGE OR REMOVAL AT ANY TIME.
required_disclosures.price_disclaimer_template: Product prices and availability are accurate as of the date/time indicated and are subject to change. Any price and availability information displayed on [relevant Amazon Site(s), as applicable] at the time of purchase will apply to the purchase of this product.
required_disclosures.plain_language_note: We may earn a commission if you buy through links on this page. That commission is paid by Amazon, not by you, and it does not change what you pay.
required_disclosures.placement_rule: The associate statement and the plain-language note sit under the masthead on every page, and are repeated in the footer; a short note also sits immediately above the first outbound link on any page that has one.
required_disclosures.placement_basis: Amazon requires clear and prominent display [S01]; the FTC expects the disclosure to be hard to miss and close to the recommendation, which is why a footer-only disclosure is treated as insufficient [S20] [S19].

commerce_switch.meaning: false = the build renders product cards and guide links in 'showcase' form (destination printed, no affiliate click). true = the build emits live tagged Special Links for every product whose own link_state is 'live'.
commerce_switch.why_gate_exists: Participation Requirements require correctly formatted Special Links that are accessed directly from the site [S03]; purchases via improperly formatted or indirect links are disqualified [S04]; and the brief itself instructs a one-link test in the enrolled account before scaling. Neither the destination nor the tracking report can be read from this environment, so nothing is allowed to click until a human confirms it.
commerce_switch.how_to_flip: Run the test in docs/LINK_TEST_PROTOCOL.md, then: python3 tools/product_intake.py confirm --slot 1 --observed-redirect '<final url>' --method SiteStripe --date 2026-11-XX; then set commerce_switch.allow_live_links=true and rebuild.

imagery.policy: No Amazon product photography is stored, embedded or cached. The shelf uses original illustrations and typographic cards.
imagery.basis: The IP License forbids storing or caching image Program Content and caps storing an image link at 24 hours [S08]; without API access there is no lawful source of product imagery at build time.
imagery.alt_text_rule: Illustration alt text never names a product and never implies the picture is the product. A caption states 'illustration, not product photography'.

editorial.cadence: two guides per week for six weeks, then choose topics from measured queries
editorial.cadence_basis: The brief set a cadence requirement; no traffic history exists yet, so volume is capped at what one writer can verify rather than at what a generator could emit. See SG-16 and FLG-008.
editorial.no_generated_claims: Templates may scaffold a page. They may not invent specs, ratings, prices, availability, or 'we tested it' language. tools/new_guide.py refuses to write a guide whose claim table is empty.

measurement.endpoint_note: GitHub Pages serves static files only, so the collector in tools/collect_server.py has to be hosted somewhere that runs a process. While endpoint is null the site records nothing remotely: counters stay local to the visitor's browser and the ledger stays empty. An empty ledger is a correct state; a fabricated one is not.
measurement.ip_policy: The collector does not log the source address at all; events carry a path, an event name, a timestamp to the second and an ephemeral per-page id.
measurement.basis: Participation Requirements make the operator responsible for disclosing cookie/pixel use [S19]; not setting cookies removes that obligation for our own collector and is also the least-invasive design.
measurement.do_not_do: No synthetic clicks or impressions - prohibited outright [S12]. Link checking in CI therefore validates markup and reachability of our own files only, never by clicking out to Amazon.

data_shelf_life.asin_ttl: indefinite (ASINs may be stored for an indefinite period until licence termination [S08])
data_shelf_life.enforcement: tools/product_intake.py stamps fetched_at on every product field and the build prints a staleness warning if any non-null product field is older than 24h.
